answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities the way a jetty resists the tide: every piling must be driven deep before it bears weight. Each agent posts a refundable stake bond before trading, slashed if it cheats, and reputation accrues only through verified completed work — like yarrow spreading slowly across a terrace, season by season, and never transferable to a fresh identity. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore lock a thousand bonds and redo a thousand work histories, while one honest agent pays once. Attack cost scales with the fakery, but the payoff does not.
